svg.title: io-guard architecture
svg.desc: How io-guard sits between Claude Code's tools and the files on disk: the hook runner calls the plugin's io server, a pipeline of checks decides, and lib does every read and write. Four coloured flows show a guarded tool call, an io tool call, session start with the heartbeat, and telemetry.
svg.text: checks what an agent sends to the file and shell tools, fixes what it safely can, and returns a structured error for the rest
IO SERVER: ONE PER SESSION, SHARED BY ITS SUBAGENTS

g.title: The agent. It picks the next tool call, and reads io-guard's refusals and context.
Claude Code's Bash and PowerShell tools. On Windows the Bash tool halves every double backslash and cuts commands near 7.8 KB.
Claude Code's Edit, Write and Read tools. io-guard conforms their input to the file's endings, BOM and indent, refuses an Edit that would join two words, and checks every write.
Fires the hook events: PreToolUse before a call, PostToolUse after it, PostToolUseFailure on an error, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit.
Permission rules, the prompt and the auto-mode classifier. They judge the input after io-guard's rewrite.
Claude Code's MCP client: one stdio connection per session to the io server, with the legacy handshake by default.
The io-guard skill: every code, its fix, and which io tool does which job, generated from the code table and the tool registry.

pyrun finds Python and runs hook.py, and pyrun.cmd starts the io server the same way on Windows. Only SessionStart and the per-turn heartbeat check start hook.py, and it warns once when the Python found is older than 3.14.
Binds each tool event to a hook.* tool on the io server (mcp_tool hooks), and SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit to pyrun.
Handles for background runs and snapshots, with stated lifetimes. The elicitor asks the user for a decision, such as a locked file.
Reads JSON-RPC from stdin, answers both MCP eras (2026-07-28 and the legacy initialize), validates _meta and maps errors.
What a check reads: the config, the platform probe, git, the file system, the clock, the session state and telemetry. Tests pass a fake one.
hook.pre_tool_use, hook.post_tool_use and hook.post_tool_use_failure: the hook events as tools, so no Python starts per call.
One ToolSpec per tool, with generated input and output schemas, annotations, and the callable names the skill prints.
hooks.entry runs one event through the pipeline. hooks.answer turns the outcome into the exact JSON the harness expects.
io.read, io.edit, io.splice, io.append, io.run, io.status, io.read_log, io.format, io.snapshot, io.restore, io.compare and io.stage.
Selects the checks for the event, orders them by layer and cost, chains their rewrites, stops at the first refusal, holds the 300 ms and 2 s budget, and fails open on a bug.
One class per concern: location, transport, bytes, stale view, read, output. Each declares its codes, its config keys and its cost.
A reader, a writer lock, four workers, a telemetry queue and a watchdog. One server serves a session and all its subagents safely.
Mechanism only, with no config and no decisions. Every disk read and write goes through it.
g.text: lib: mechanism only, and every read and write goes through it
profile anchors shell paths git locks proc results config rules telemetry bytes and atomic writes

g.title: The page io.dashboard serves on 127.0.0.1, behind a token: checks on or off, rewrite modes and lists, in your config or the project's, written through io.config. Its Stats switch shows the telemetry by day and code, and report.py --html writes the same stats into one file.

io-guard's folder, ~/.claude/io-guard, one per user and shared by every copy of the plugin: config.json, probe.json, snapshots, handles, locks, the edit journal, one telemetry file per session, and the heartbeat.
g.text: config, probe, snapshots, handles, locks, telemetry, heartbeat

g.title: The session scratchpad: command bodies moved out of heredocs, and the logs of io.run.
Read for tracked files, status and hunks. io.stage writes the index only, and nothing ever commits.
The files the agent works on. Every io tool writes them atomically, under a lock that two sessions share.

g.text: What happens to a rewritten command
Default in auto and dontAsk. Denied, with the fixed
command as the fix. The model reruns it, so the
Default in default, acceptEdits and plan. You see
the fixed command and approve it.
Default in bypassPermissions. Runs at once, and no
Set per permission mode in config.json, with io.config,
or on the dashboard. File-tool fixes keep the prompt.
When a check is slow or broken
Past 300 ms the checks that run a subprocess are skipped.
Past 2 s every remaining check is skipped, and the call
goes ahead with what was decided. Both are settings.
A check that crashes is skipped and logged, the call runs,
and you get one warning per session. A guard bug never
If the io server dies, the next prompt says so once. Claude
Code does not restart it, so a new session brings it back.

svg.text: Opened in a browser: pick a flow to follow it, press Play to walk it step by step, and hover or focus a box to read what it does. Docs: docs/design/architecture.md.
